All per share amounts presented in this press release are on a diluted per common share basis unless stated otherwise.\n\nCOMPANY HIGHLIGHTS:\n\nFor the three months ended September 30, 2026:\n\n- Net income available to common stockholders was $403.9 million, or $0.43 per share\n- Adjusted Funds from Operations (\"AFFO\") increased 3.7% to $1.12 per share, compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025\n- Invested $2.6 billion; our Pro-Rata Share was $2.2 billion at an Initial Weighted Average Cash Yield of 6.8%\n- Net Debt to Annualized Pro Forma Adjusted EBITDAre was 5.4x\n- Achieved a Rent Recapture Rate of 103.5% on properties re-leased\n- Expanded our private capital platform into Europe through a strategic joint venture with KKR, supported by an initial €528.0 million investment\n- Issued $1.0 billion aggregate principal amount of 3.750% convertible senior notes due August 2031\n\nCEO Comments\n\n\"We delivered another quarter of strong operating performance, reflecting the resilience of Realty Income's business model, the quality of our portfolio, and the consistent execution of our team,\" said Sumit Roy, President and Chief Executive Officer of Realty Income. \"As a result, we are raising our 2026 AFFO per share guidance to $4.45–$4.46 while reaffirming our $10.0 billion investment volume target, which is supported by a well-funded balance sheet.\"\n\n\"We have deliberately expanded our sources of capital and global investment capabilities, positioning us to prudently allocate capital. This quarter, we funded investments at a realized leverage-neutral spread of approximately 170 basis points and have fully prefunded our equity needs for the remainder of the year. Disclosure\n\nDividend was 74.4% of AFFO in Q2 2026.\n\nQuick Answer\n\nRealty Income (NYSE: O, SEC CIK 726728) paid $0.8115 a share in dividends in the second quarter of 2026 against $1.09 of adjusted funds from operations (AFFO) per diluted share, 74.4% of AFFO (our arithmetic; the company's release says 74.5% on a rounded $0.812). The monthly dividend declared in July 2026 is $0.2710, or $3.252 a year. Operating cash flow was 1.33 times the distributions paid in the first half of 2026 (our arithmetic). Two things the quote pages leave out: Q1 2026 AFFO of $1.13 included $40.2 million of lease termination income, and the quarterly dividend raises are now $0.0005 a month (0.2%) against Q2 AFFO-per-share growth of 3.8% over a year. As of the June 30, 2026 10-Q (filed August 6): 15,588 properties, 1,798 clients, 98.8% occupancy, a weighted average remaining lease term of 8.6 years (9.3 at December 31, 2024), and $30.99 billion of debt at 5.4 times EBITDAre. 23.6% of annualized base rent expires by the end of 2029 and 20.5% of rent comes from Europe, 15.0% from the United Kingdom (our arithmetic). A $650.0 million 4.125% note matures today, October 15, 2026. All figures are as of October 15, 2026; the Q3 2026 10-Q has not been filed.\n\n### Key Takeaways\n\n- The dividend is covered on AFFO and the cushion is not growing the way the headline raises suggest. Paid as a share of AFFO per share (our arithmetic) the last seven quarters were 75.3%, 75.1%, 76.7%, 74.7%, 74.9%, 71.7% and 74.4%. The annualized dividend went from $3.228 at June 30, 2025 to $3.252 at June 30, 2026, up 0.7%, while Q2 AFFO per share rose 3.8%. On the August 5 guidance midpoint of $4.445 the $3.252 is 73.2% (our arithmetic).\n- Q1 2026 was flattered. AFFO per share was $1.13 in Q1 and $1.09 in Q2; lease termination income was $40.2 million in Q1 and $1.0 million in Q2 ($41.2 million in the half, against $2.8 million a year earlier). Taking all of it out of AFFO (our arithmetic) leaves about $1.09 for Q1 and $2.18 for the half, up 3.4% rather than 5.2%. Guidance for termination income was raised from $30-40 million to $45-50 million, and AFFO guidance from $4.38-4.42 to $4.44-4.45.\n- 23.6% of annualized base rent (ABR), $1.25 billion of $5.28 billion, expires from now through 2029, and 39.3% through 2031 (our arithmetic). The 2026 bucket fell from $116.5 million at March 31 to $78.2 million at June 30, 2026, and the through-2029 share from 25.7% to 23.6%. Expiry is not vacancy: of 480 lease expirations in Q2, 385 were re-leased to the same client, 34 to a new client and 45 were sold vacant, and re-leased units paid 102.7% of the old rent.\n- The portfolio is getting shorter and bigger. The weighted average remaining lease term has fallen every quarter, from 9.3 years (Q4 2024) to 8.6 years; clients rose from 1,565 to 1,798; Europe is 20.5% of base rent (20.3% at March 31). Rent recapture, 107.4% in Q4 2024, was 102.7% in Q2 2026. Real-estate impairments were $54.2 million in Q2 against $142.3 million a year earlier.\n- Debt is $31.0 billion, all of the notes unsecured, at a 3.9% average rate and 5.8 years to maturity. $9.49 billion of notes (37.3%) fall due from 2026 to 2029 (our arithmetic), including $950.0 million this autumn. Since January the company has issued $862.5 million of 3.500% and $1.0 billion of 3.750% convertible notes, and recast its revolver to $5.5 billion. Fitch assigned an A rating on August 3, 2026, alongside A3 (Moody's) and A- (S&P).\n- Growth now runs through lending and new equity. The loan book was $3.30 billion at June 30, up 96% in six months from $1.68 billion, with $1.26 billion of unsecured and mezzanine loans at 9.1% to fund data center and industrial investments. Shares outstanding rose 3.5% in a year to 946.2 million, and 22.5 million more are sold forward on the at-the-market (ATM) program for about $1.3 billion.\n- Against a non-traded net-lease vehicle (Blue Owl's ORENT), the cost and coverage numbers differ sharply. ORENT's adviser compensation was 41.5% of its first-half distributions and operating cash flow covered 88.8% of them; Realty Income's total G&A was 7.7% of its first-half cash distributions (our arithmetic; not a like-for-like fee comparison, explained below).\n\nCSV · 404 rows\n\nRealty Income (O): dividend vs AFFO by quarter, lease expirations, clients, debt maturities, loans and share count\n\n404 rows from Realty Income's FY2025 10-K, 10-Qs for Q3 2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026, seven earnings releases, the August 2026 8-Ks and ORENT's Q2 2026 10-Q: AFFO and dividends by quarter, portfolio statistics, lease expirations by year, top 20 clients, industries, geography, debt, loans and equity.\n\nRealty Income (O) dividend, AFFO, lease expiration and debt numbers, as of October 1","highlights":["arithmetic), $950.0 million of it this autumn.
